chunks: A Day on which human beings would be like so many scattered moths,

key_terms.الْفَرَاشِ: The moths (small insects that flutter erratically)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by people being like scattered moths on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the metaphor of 'scattered moths' (al-farash al-mash al-mabthuth) emphasizes not only the physical dispersion but also the spiritual disorientation of those whose deeds are light, contrasting them with the steadfastness of the believers. This imagery serves as a vivid reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the inevitable accountability before Allah, urging reflection on one's spiritual state before the Day of Reckoning.
